subject: AcreetionOS Update — June 24, 2026
body:
Emacs 31.1 has just been released, and our community is already exploring the new features and improvements it brings, including the removal of the old GUI. This update is a great example of how our Arch-based foundation keeps our users up-to-date with the latest software releases. 

Development
The development team has been focused on fine-tuning our continuous integration pipeline, with recent commits like the use of per-pipeline staging directories to avoid publish races between concurrent builds, which you can read more about on our changelog page at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html. This work is crucial to ensuring our release process is reliable and efficient, and we're excited to see the impact it will have on our users.

Community
Our community has also been discussing the latest security updates, including those for AlmaLinux and the recent stable kernel set, which includes versions 7.1.10 and 6.18.46. You can find more information about these updates on our wiki page at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html, and learn how to apply them to your system using our documentation at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html. If you're looking for the latest ISO, you can find it at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html.

Tip of the day
If you're looking to get the most out of your AcreetionOS setup, be sure to check out our documentation at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html, which includes guides on everything from installation to configuration and troubleshooting. With the latest Emacs release and our ongoing pipeline improvements, there's never been a better time to explore what AcreetionOS has to offer, and you can learn more about our project at https://acreetionos.org/.
